name: Aminotrimethylene phosphonic acid
description: Aminotrimethylene phosphonic acid (CAS 6419-19-8 ), commercially known as ATMP, is a phosphonate chelating agent used across industrial water and process chemistry. It controls scale deposition and inhibits corrosion in systems where mineral buildup and metal degradation are operational concerns. In water treatment, ATMP prevents calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, and barium sulfate scale in cooling towers, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems by threshold inhibition and crystal modification. Oil and gas operations rely on it as a scale inhibitor in oilfield injection water and produced water handling, where mineral precipitation can block pipelines and reduce flow efficiency. Textile and paper processing use ATMP to sequester hardness ions in process water, preventing interference with dyeing, bleaching, and pulp treatment chemistry in various industrial environments. In metalworking and mining, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and chelating agent in circulating water systems and mineral processing circuits to ensure long-term equipment durability and performance. ATMP is supplied as a liquid solution, typically at 50% active content, and as a solid crystalline powder for applications requiring concentrated or dry formulations for specific manufacturing needs. Technical grade is the standard offering across most industrial segments. Specifications are typically aligned with industry performance benchmarks rather than pharmacopeial standards like USP or FCC . Given its primarily industrial end-use profile, the material is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols to maintain high efficiency in large-scale cooling and heating applications.
